producer_report.summary: An invocation's measured tokens and the gate's reconciliation rule now use one definition: the sum of the result event's `modelUsage` over all models. Root cause: `parse_result` took tokens from the event's top-level `usage`, which counts the main thread only, while `check_invocation` compared them with `modelUsage`, which includes subagents. Job 2fsa recorded 6/3136/275219/3821 against a `modelUsage` of 90/52656/3634696/134508. Fixes: (1) `parse_result` in stream.rs sets `ResultEvent.usage` to the `modelUsage` sum and falls back to top-level `usage` only when `modelUsage` is absent. (2) The one definition is a doc comment on `ResultEvent.usage` and on `AgentOutput.usage`. (3) The result-to-`AgentOutput` mapping moved out of the driver's `invoke` into the new `claude::output_from_result`, so the driver and the end-to-end test share it. (4) `check_invocation` in reconcile.rs compares the record's tokens with the sum over all models. It still accepts the legacy shape, where only the requested model's entry was recorded, and it still flags a missing requested-model entry. (5) The record's token basis string now says `modelUsage`. (6) CHANGELOG.md records the fix. New tests: stream.rs (2), the claude.rs stand-in (1), reconcile.rs (1) and invocation.rs (2); the acceptance-criteria table is in criteria_check below. The end-to-end tests are in athena-core, which depends on agent and gate. They run the result line through `StreamState`, then `output_from_result`, `Athena::invocation_record` and `check_invocation`. The negative case is a result event with top-level usage and no `modelUsage`; I also tamper with the 2fsa record's output count. I did not touch landing_tests.rs or fake.rs: no change was needed there and the full suite passes.

criteria_check.criterion: Run cargo test: a named end-to-end test feeds a result event through the stream parser and the claude driver (fake script) or the invocation constructor. Its top-level usage differs from modelUsage (main thread plus subagent usage on the requested model, using 90/52656/3634696/134508 against 6/3136/275219/3821). It then runs check_invocation on the resulting record and asserts there is no Reconciliation violation.
criteria_check.evidence: Test `a_result_with_subagent_usage_reconciles_end_to_end` in crates/athena-core/src/invocation.rs: StreamState::on_line, then claude::output_from_result, then Athena::invocation_record, then check_invocation. It asserts the record holds 90/52656/3634696/134508 and that there are no Reconciliation violations. Run: cargo test --locked -p athena-core --lib invocation::. Passed in the full `cargo test --locked -q` run.

criteria_check.criterion: Run cargo test: a named negative test builds the record from a result event whose totals really disagree with modelUsage, through the same path. It asserts that check_invocation returns a Reconciliation violation.
criteria_check.evidence: Test `a_result_whose_totals_disagree_with_model_usage_is_flagged_end_to_end` in invocation.rs. It uses a result event with top-level usage and no modelUsage, and the 2fsa record with its output count altered to 3136. Both give exactly one Reconciliation violation. Passed.

criteria_check.criterion: One definition of an invocation's measured tokens is stated in a doc comment (on ResultEvent.usage and AgentOutput.usage in lib.rs). The invocation record and the gate's reconcile rule both use it.
criteria_check.evidence: Doc comments are on `ResultEvent.usage` in stream.rs and `AgentOutput.usage` in lib.rs. `parse_result` sums modelUsage; `output_from_result` and `invocation_record` carry it; `check_invocation` in reconcile.rs sums per-model tokens. Tests: stream.rs `measured_usage_is_the_sum_of_model_usage_not_the_top_level_usage`, claude.rs `a_run_with_subagents_measures_the_model_usage_sum`, reconcile.rs `tokens_are_the_sum_over_all_models_and_the_legacy_shape_passes`.

open_issues: The legacy tolerance in `check_invocation` accepts a record whose tokens equal the requested model's entry alone, even when several models ran. A genuine single-model-only mismatch in that shape is not flagged, which is intentional. records/ was absent, so I could not check older records against the new rule.
landing_tests.rs and fake.rs were listed as deliverables but needed no change.
learnings: A job's tests run under the nested-run marker, so a core test cannot use the real Claude driver. The end-to-end test uses `claude::output_from_result`, which the driver also uses.
`Athena` can be built in a core unit test with `FakeAgentDriver`, `CountingPinner`, `Config::parse(include_str!("../../../athena.toml"))` and `Redactor::new(&builtin_config())`.
Once tokens are derived from modelUsage, a disagreement can only be reached by a result with no modelUsage, a missing requested-model entry, or a tampered record.
